problem_description: Compare 11-dimensional cyclic signal-control plans for three controlled intersections in the Cologne3 SUMO scenario.

simulator.name: SUMO with the RESCO Cologne3 environment

randomness.policy: SUMO randomization enabled; no common fixed seed was supplied across candidate evaluations

objective.name: total_vehicle_waiting_time
objective.definition: Sum the SUMO tripinfo waitingTime attribute over all non-ghost vehicles written at the end of the configured simulation window. For vehicles unfinished at the end, include their waitingTime accumulated up to that point.

control_logic.plan_type: cyclic sequence of RESCO green actions per controlled signal
control_logic.requested_duration: Candidate values request seconds of holding their mapped green action.
control_logic.effective_duration: The controller acts every 5 seconds and holds an action for ceil(requested_seconds / 5) control steps.
control_logic.fixed_elements: The network, demand, green-action states, action order, and RESCO/SUMO transition behavior remain fixed across candidates.

constraints: Every requested duration must remain within its declared bound.
Only the holding durations of the 11 mapped green actions vary.

demand_interpretation.format: The route file contains 4,494 SUMO <vehicle> records with an explicit edge sequence in each nested <route> element.
demand_interpretation.routing: The supplied edge sequence is a scenario fact. Runtime lane choices, speeds, queues, signal-arrival times and unfinished status are simulator outcomes not provided to the Agent.

available_information: SUMO configuration, network and explicit vehicle routes
traffic-light action states and movement descriptions
candidate parameter values and pair indices
simulation time window and the non-fixed randomization policy used to collect private truth
limitations: The Agent may not run SUMO and receives no queues, delays, objective values or truth labels.
Preferences are static model-based priors compared against one randomized rollout per candidate.
No common SUMO seed was fixed across candidate evaluations, so small objective gaps may contain label noise.
One rollout per candidate does not estimate expected performance across alternative SUMO random realizations.
